reason: Broad 'supply most' overclaim; synchrotron MX is the main source of PDB structures but XFEL contributes little by count. Not strength 3.

fix.summary: Synchrotron macromolecular crystallography and SAXS supply the large majority of experimental protein crystal structures; XFEL serial femtosecond crystallography adds room-temperature and time-resolved structures of small or radiation-sensitive crystals.

reason: Phase-contrast imaging is not a precursor of CT reconstruction; microCT is a direct application. Rephrase.

fix.summary: Coherent synchrotron beams enable propagation-based and grating phase-contrast imaging and microCT of soft tissue, which is mostly preclinical; clinical translation is limited.

reason: Superconducting gravimeters are not atom interferometers or quantum sensing in this sense; and the seismology node is a weak fit for gravimetry. Narrow and downgrade.

fix.summary: Atom-interferometric gravimeters measure absolute g for geodesy, hydrology and subsurface density mapping, complementing seismic structure; field use is emerging.

reason: Same spin-precession physics is a shared mechanism, but the SQUID/ULF-MRI clause is loose; MEG is not MRI. Tighten.

fix.summary: MRI, NV and atomic magnetometers all rely on coherent spin precession at the Larmor frequency; Ramsey and spin-echo sequences are the same Bloch-equation protocols. SQUIDs and SERF sensors also enable ultra-low-field MRI.

reason: SiPMs are silicon avalanche photodiode arrays in Geiger mode; CdZnTe is a direct detector, not avalanche.

fix.summary: Silicon photomultipliers (Geiger-mode avalanche photodiode arrays) read out LYSO scintillators in time-of-flight PET; CdZnTe semiconductor detectors directly convert gamma rays in some SPECT cameras.

reason: Shear-wave speed c_s=sqrt(mu/rho) holds for elastic, not viscoelastic, tissue; the link to cell-scale mechanics is indirect.

fix.summary: Elastography infers tissue shear modulus from shear-wave speed, c_s=√(μ/ρ) in the elastic limit; the same stiffness governs mechanotransduction studied in cell and tissue mechanics, though the scales differ.

reason: Not an identity: Kramers/TST apply to both but folding funnels are high-dimensional and the prefactor is not simple; map is approximate. Mechanism fits.

fix.summary: Folding landscapes and chemical potential energy surfaces both use Kramers and transition-state barrier-crossing rate theory and funnel concepts; force spectroscopy extends rates via Bell-Evans.

reason: Kinetic proofreading is a theory (Hopfield, Ninio) not 'observed directly' by single-molecule counting; single-molecule methods test it indirectly.

fix.summary: Gene-expression noise and kinetic proofreading are stochastic-kinetics ideas; single-molecule counting (smFISH, enzyme turnover) measures noise and tests proofreading indirectly.

reason: Analogy valid but generic; name the shared bifurcation structure, keep strength 1 and note Stommel bistability.

fix.summary: Both gene circuits (toggle switches) and climate (Stommel AMOC bistability, ice-albedo feedback) are modelled as bistable nonlinear systems with saddle-node bifurcations and noise-induced transitions.

reason: smFRET is a method built on Förster theory, not a descendant of Raman spectroscopy; strength 3 inflated.

fix.summary: smFRET applies Förster dipole-dipole energy transfer, E=1/(1+(r/R0)^6), and fluorescence photophysics from molecular spectroscopy to measure 2-10 nm distances and conformational dynamics in single molecules.

reason: Map should be the Bell form k(F)=k0 exp(F x‡/kBT); Jarzynski/Crooks belong to fluctuation theorems, not this pair; chem-physics side is barrier-crossing rate theory. Fine as mechanism, strength 2.

fix.summary: Pulling experiments measure unfolding barriers via Kramers and Bell-Evans force-dependent rates, k(F)=k0 exp(F x‡/kBT), the same rate theory used in reaction dynamics.

reason: Generic overlap with no named technique or consequence; OCT is not used in single-molecule tracking and the name misdescribes the content.
Correct mechanism, but CO2 forcing logarithm and band structure are the key consequence; also wording 'feed' fine. Specify map.

fix.summary: CO2, H2O and CH4 vibration-rotation bands (e.g. CO2 bending mode at 15 μm), with line strengths from spectroscopy databases such as HITRAN, set the opacity in line-by-line radiative transfer and hence greenhouse forcing.

reason: Not an identity: shared equations but ocean has boundaries, different stratification and no moist physics; kind should be mechanism. Western boundary currents are not a mirror of jets.

fix.summary: Atmosphere and ocean share rotating stratified fluid dynamics: geostrophic balance, Rossby waves, Ekman layers and baroclinic instability, with different deformation radii, boundaries and forcing.

reason: Geodynamo is in the seismology node, but atmosphere link is a loose analogy; Taylor-Proudman applies to all, though Ekman number in the core is ~1e-15 and Lorentz force matters.

fix.breaks: Geodynamo has Lorentz forces, a much lower Ekman number (~1e-15) and no free surface or moist physics.

reason: Map ΔT=λΔF is wrong: with λ in W m⁻² K⁻¹ it is ΔT=ΔF/λ at equilibrium.

fix.summary: Ocean heat uptake, a large heat capacity C, delays warming relative to equilibrium ΔT=ΔF/λ, so transient response lags; AMOC redistributes heat.

reason: Tsunamis are earthquake-generated shallow-water waves; tides are not generated by earthquakes. Wording conflates them.

fix.summary: Seafloor earthquake displacement is the source of tsunamis, which propagate as shallow-water waves at c=√(gh); source seismology sets the initial condition.

reason: Not an identity: same elastic wave equation but different regimes (ray theory, frequency, attenuation); kind should be method transfer.

fix.summary: Full-waveform inversion, developed in seismology, now also images tissue with ultrasound; both invert elastic wave equation ρü=∇·σ, though frequencies and scales differ.

reason: Too generic; photoacoustic reconstruction claim is loose. Narrow to named framework.

fix.summary: MTF, point-spread function and contrast-to-noise frameworks apply across MRI, ultrasound and OCT; MRI k-space and Fourier-domain OCT both acquire Fourier-domain data.

record.name: Linacs and proton accelerators in therapy
record.summary: Medical linacs and cyclotron/synchrotron proton and carbon-ion sources apply RF acceleration and beam transport from accelerator physics to deliver MV photon and Bragg-peak beams.
